findings.reason: §3's write paths and done-when gain the three followup-body sites, or the section states why a followup body is exempt where a comment body is not.
findings.text: the widened term is refused only where `_refuse_forged_body_structure` already runs (`insert_section` at reckon/_store.py:1074, `append_evidence` at reckon/_store.py:1202) plus the comments branch §3 adds at reckon/_store.py:3798, so every followup-body write still accepts the term: `append_to_list` at reckon/_store.py:2381-2389, the `followups` append op at reckon/_store.py:3760-3777, and the `followups.<id>.<field>` set at reckon/_store.py:3482-3486; §1 measured the phrases in "followup bodies and close comments", so §3 would close half the population it cites — the audit already warns at reckon/doccheck.py:1728, so only the write-time refusal is missing there

findings.reason: the plan must name the one function in reckon/evidence.py that derives the renderable-id set and have both callers use it, which changes the module boundary and the refusal's write path.
findings.text: §4 defines "every id this synthesis renders" (plan section ids, `outcome`, the plan's comment keys, the current ledger runs' `section` keys, all normalised through `_section_key`) twice: once for the carry-forward and rendered-id exclusion in `synthesize_landed_record`, and again for the new anchor refusal in `_apply_evidence_appends` at reckon/_store.py:1230, which the plan itself says "gains the comment-key and ledger reads the refusal needs"; two independent computations of one set, in two modules, whose agreement is the entire correctness condition the section rests on

findings.reason: a `summary: str | None` (or equivalent) parameter on `_render_document` yields the same shell from one owner, and the plan's write path and four negative controls are written against the second renderer instead.
findings.text: `_landed_record_shell` currently delegates to `evidence._render_document` (reckon/evidence.py:329) and the record head it emits — doctype, `docs-project`, `reckon-type`, `plan-slug` at reckon/evidence.py:413, `plan-title`, `plan-evidence-for` at reckon/evidence.py:416, `<h1>`, stylesheets, `<main>` at reckon/evidence.py:428-446 — is owned by that renderer; §2 removes the delegation (its negative control is "restoring the shell's delegation") and so re-emits that head beside its owner, differing only by the count sentence at reckon/evidence.py:406-408 and the verdict meta at reckon/evidence.py:417, with no statement of why `_render_document` cannot take those two as parameters

findings.reason: §4 should have `synthesize_landed_record` call `_evidence_record_path` (or move the accessor to evidence.py) in the same commit, and the section's write paths should say so.
findings.text: the landed-record path is derived inline as `docs_dir / "evidence" / "archive" / f"{plan_slug}-landed.html"` while its owner `_evidence_record_path` (reckon/_store.py:1172-1174) computes the same path for the append writer at reckon/_store.py:1249, and a third copy is spelled inside the refusal at reckon/_store.py:4577; §2 and §4 edit both writers and §4's new refusal makes the two paths interact (an append written through one path is compared against ids rendered through the other), so a placement change in the owner silently writes or refuses in the wrong file

findings.reason: the section must either account for the added surface or collapse the two lists into one, which changes the dataclass, the printer and the done-when cases seven, eight and eleven.

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §4 needs "the ids a synthesis can render" in two modules (the carry-forward in `reckon/evidence.py`, the anchor refusal in `reckon/_store.py`) and names no single function that derives it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan edits both writers of the landed-record path but leaves the path itself duplicated, with `reckon/_store.py:1172` owning it and `reckon/evidence.py:674` re-deriving it inline.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 2360, cli_options 465, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 23; §4 grows `EvidenceSynthesisResult` by two fields and adds an anchor refusal without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the machinery it searched accurately (`doccheck._DEFERRED_WORK_TERM`, `_store._prose_deferred_work_term`, `evidence._render_document`, `_overall_verdict`), but its census of the store's deferred-work refusal stops at one call site and leaves the three followup-body writers unwired, which is the other population its own §1 evidence names.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2's `_landed_record_shell` becomes a second rendering of the record head that differs from `evidence._render_document` only by dropping one sentence and one meta, and the plan never says why that renderer cannot take the omission as a parameter.
